block: The P0 remedy is built, green and live-proven, but the push to the qhstate origin was refused by this host's classifier guard, so the fix reaches no lane.
background: MEASURED 2026-09-05T16:51Z on SHIRAS. Branch 095-m6-send-spool, commit fdb823c9, in the qhstate object store via a worktree off develop. Suite 93/93 green (85 baseline re-measured first, 8 new).

LIVE PROOF with the receiver ACTIVE: 'sent (stamped by the running receiver, seq=12)', exit 0; the receiver logged 'spool drained ...send seq=12 outcome=Sent'; the frame landed in the peer inbox at 16:51.
OriginLock and FR-015 are unchanged in substance - still exactly one stamper per origin. The holder drains a ticket spool instead of refusing a competitor.

THE PUSH WAS REFUSED. Three outward actions were refused by the guard this session (qhstate push, a direct read of the peer's script, one shared-volume listing). The GLPNET push succeeded, so the guard is repo-scoped, not blanket.
The branch is already on this machine in qhstate's own object store, so no push is needed for the owning lane to merge it.
impact_if_unanswered: Every lane in the fleet, including this one, keeps trading receive for send: to publish anything a lane must stop its own M6 receiver, send, and restart it. The incentive to leave receivers down - which doctor rewards, since it reports MET either way - stays in place.

options.label: shiras-qhstate merges it locally
options.consequence: No push needed; the owning lane merges to develop and rebuilds Release. Depends on a live shiras-qhstate session, which has WIP in that tree and must merge without disturbing it.

options.label: Engineer grants the push permission
options.consequence: Normal GitFlow via PR, but widens a guard that has refused three outward actions this session, possibly deliberately.

options.label: Deploy the patched build to this lane only
options.consequence: This lane sends immediately but runs a binary no other lane has - the divergence R-B was ruled to end - and the build is session-ephemeral.

options.label: Leave it; keep the stop-send-start dance
options.consequence: P0 stays open fleet-wide and every lane keeps trading receive for send. It FORECLOSES the 20:00Z subroot cutover being verifiable from inside M6: with sends only possible while the receiver is down, no lane can confirm its own post-cutover reachability without going deaf again, so the window's success would have to be taken on report rather than measured.

recommendation.because: The branch is already in qhstate's own object store on this machine, so the owning lane needs no push at all - the blocked action is not on its critical path. R-B already put this code in qhstate's tree, and a lane merging its own repo is the smallest act that reaches every lane. Deploying locally would give this lane a binary nobody else has, which is exactly the divergence R-B was ruled to end.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled the owning lane merges branch 095-m6-send-spool (fdb823c9) from its own object store and rebuilds. shiras-glpnet claims no ownership of the file; R-B stands.

block: The 20:00Z M6 subroot cutover was proposed under lazy consensus by a lane, but the fleet's designated coordinator for exactly this kind of fleetwide act is yng-broker/yng-guardian.
background: R-A2 (15:10Z) ruled the subroot cutover and proposed 2026-09-05T20:00Z, objections by 18:00Z.
It cannot be done lane by lane: a peer is addressed by its directory under the root, so an early mover is unreachable to every lane that has not moved, and its sends fail closed.
The engineer's standing rule designates yng-broker/yng-guardian on each of the 4 hosts as the PBFT leader-elector and fleetwide coordinator.
NOT MEASURED: whether yng-broker is actually running on any host. This lane has not probed it.
impact_if_unanswered: Either the window passes with no one calling it, or a lane calls a fleetwide restart it has no standing to call - and a partial cutover splits the carrier in two, which must be completed rather than reverted.

options.label: Hold 20:00Z, yng-broker owns the window
options.consequence: Keeps the time and puts coordination where the standing rule puts it; requires yng-broker to be live and to accept, which is unmeasured.

options.label: Hold 20:00Z, shiras-glpnet coordinates
options.consequence: A lane coordinating a fleetwide restart is the shape prior rulings moved away from; this lane cannot verify which lanes restarted.

options.label: Defer the cutover
options.consequence: The R-A1 tilde filter remains the whole remedy - measured working 44/44 this session - but it is a convention every fanout must remember.

recommendation.because: The time is already published and lazy consensus is running, so moving it costs more than keeping it. What should change is who calls it: the standing rule designates yng-broker/yng-guardian as the fleetwide coordinator, and a fleetwide synchronised restart is precisely that role. This lane withdraws its own claim to coordinate rather than defend it.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled the 20:00Z window stands and yng-broker/yng-guardian owns it. shiras-glpnet's coordination proposal is withdrawn in favour of the broker; this lane complies with the window the broker calls.

block: The roadmap's ranked next differs from the features the engineer's directives name as today's must-haves, and three of those are promoted but unscored so they cannot rank at all.
background: MEASURED 2026-09-05T16:03Z. buildkit-roadmap next returns per-host-toolchain-and-environment-contract at rank 24, WSJF 3.60.
m6-send-spool-hardening was captured, scored WSJF 6.50 / RICE 1068.75 and promoted this session; it ranks #9 and is the highest scored open item after the federation-identity cluster.

pbft-leader-election, qhsm-virtual-terminals and iroh-quic-transport are all promoted with NO score, so they sort to the bottom of a WSJF-descending board regardless of the directives naming them critical.
104-wp02-quic-listener-service merged into develop this session, so iroh work here would overlap another lane's just-landed delivery.
impact_if_unanswered: The lane either follows a ranked board that does not reflect today's stated priorities, or abandons the board - and an unscored promoted feature is invisible to every ranking the fleet uses.

options.label: m6-send-spool-hardening
options.consequence: Hardens a remedy already measured green and live rather than opening a new front: doctor blindness, operator verbs, back-pressure, ticket-index compaction, four-host proof. Does not advance PBFT or terminals.

options.label: pbft-leader-election
options.consequence: Directly addresses a stated automatic-failure criterion, but needs other lanes participating over a carrier they currently cannot send on.

options.label: qhsm-virtual-terminals
options.consequence: Largest scope, no spec dir; the L0 sharing rule puts the core in yngenios, so this lane would own a part.

recommendation.because: It is the highest-scored open item after the federation-identity cluster, it hardens something already measured green and live-proven today rather than opening a new front, and it removes the doctor blindness that let this defect hide - a compliance instrument that reports MET while sending is impossible will hide the next one too. PBFT depends on a carrier lanes currently cannot send on; iroh overlaps 104-wp02 merged today.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled m6-send-spool-hardening is this lane's mandatory next era, ahead of the board's rank-24 recommendation. Residual finding recorded: pbft-leader-election, qhsm-virtual-terminals and iroh-quic-transport are promoted but UNSCORED, so they are invisible to every WSJF ranking the fleet uses - they need scoring before any board can reflect the directives.
